questions.q: In a Fabric notebook, how can pandas read a file from the notebook's default lakehouse?
options: Only after exporting it to a local laptop
Through the mount point /lakehouse/default/, for example pd.read_csv on a path under it
Only with a Spark job definition
By calling mlflow.read_file()
questions.explain: Per the Fabric docs, the default lakehouse is mounted at /lakehouse/default/ in notebooks, so the pandas API can read and write its files directly.

questions.q: Which tool do you use in Fabric to track experiments and register models?
options: A Fabric-only tracking library with no relation to open source
SQL Server Agent
MLflow, the same API you used on your laptop and on Databricks
Only the Azure ML SDK v2
questions.explain: Fabric has a built-in MLflow experience. Calls such as set_experiment, start_run, log_metric and register_model work the same way.

questions.q: What does the docs say PREDICT requires of a model?
options: It must be saved in MLflow format with its signature populated
It must be a deep learning model
It must use multi-tensor inputs
It must be trained on Spark only
questions.explain: PREDICT needs MLflow-format models with populated signatures, supports listed flavors such as sklearn and XGBoost, and does not support multi-tensor inputs or outputs.

questions.q: Why did the lesson build the signature from pipe.predict(Xte) instead of predict_proba?
options: predict_proba cannot be logged in MLflow
A signature is optional, so it does not matter
Fabric only accepts integer outputs
The signature should describe what the logged model's predict() actually returns, and here that is class labels
questions.explain: The pyfunc model returns labels from predict(), so a signature built from probabilities would misdescribe the output. Keep the signature and behavior consistent.

questions.q: After batch predictions are written to a lakehouse table, how can Power BI show them without a data refresh, per the docs?
options: By emailing a CSV export
By using Direct Lake mode, which reads the data directly from OneLake
By copying the table into a laptop Excel file
It cannot; Power BI cannot read lakehouse tables
questions.explain: Direct Lake mode reads data directly from OneLake without copying it into the semantic model, so fresh predictions appear without a load or refresh.
